mainTopic: Why רב requires a גט when a man made קידושין on a condition and then married her without mentioning it, why the רב–שמואל dispute appears in two cases, and a משנה that seems to refute שמואל.
overview: This amud first pins down רב's real reason for requiring a גט when a man made קידושין on a condition and later married her without mentioning it. The reason is not that he dropped his condition. It is that a person does not want his relations to be בעילת זנות, so he intends them as real קידושין. The גמרא then asks why this dispute needs to be stated, since רב and שמואל already argue about the same idea. That other case is a קטנה who never did מיאון, grew up, and married someone else. The גמרא answers צריכא, in both directions. From the קטנה case alone, we might think רב agrees with שמואל when there is a condition. From the conditional case alone, we might think שמואל agrees with רב when there is no condition. Finally, the גמרא brings a משנה: a woman married without mention of a condition who turns out to have vows leaves without a כתובה. The גמרא infers from this that she still needs a גט, and suggests that this is a strong refutation of שמואל.

steps.title: The true reason behind רב's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב's reason is not that the husband waived his condition. It is that a person does not want his relations with a woman to be בעילת זנות, so he intends them to make a real קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't say רב's reason is that, since he married her without specifying anything, he completely gave up his condition. Rather, רב's reason is that a person does not turn his relations into licentious relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects one possible explanation of רב's ruling and replaces it with the correct one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband had fully dropped his condition, he would owe her a full כתובה. Instead, רב's reason is that he does not want his בעילה to be זנות, so he means it as an unconditional קידושין, which is why she needs a גט. The condition itself was not erased, so this reason does not mean he gave it up.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't say (don't explain it this way)
He married her without specifying (without repeating the condition)
He completely waived it
A condition
Licentious relations, outside of marriage

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two reasons. Under the rejected reason the condition is gone completely. Under the accepted reason he only makes sure the בעילה counts as קידושין, and the condition was never given up.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle 'אין אדם עושה בעילתו בעילת זנות' is the key idea that the rest of this section examines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the reasoning behind רב's ruling from the earlier discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's reason is that a person does not intend his בעילה to be זנות, so he means it as קידושין. It is not that he waived his condition.

steps.title: Haven't רב and שמואל already argued about this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רב and שמואל already disagree about this same principle in the case of a קטנה who did not do מיאון, grew up, and married someone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they already argued about this once. It was stated: a minor girl who did not refuse her husband grew up and then went and married another man. רב said she does not need a גט from the second husband. שמואל said she does need a גט from the second husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the dispute needs to be stated here, since the same argument already appears in another case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the קטנה case, רב holds that once she grew up, the first husband's relations with her made a real קידושין, because a person does not intend זנות. So her second marriage means nothing. שמואל disagrees, so the second marriage takes effect. Since this is the same principle, recording the dispute again seems repetitive.

A bill of divorce from the second husband

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רב's reason is clear, the גמרא points out that the same reasoning already appears in another dispute.
steps.kashyaTarget: Why the רב–שמואל dispute about a conditional קידושין followed by an unspecified marriage needs to be stated at all.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The principle 'אין אדם עושה בעילתו בעילת זנות' is already disputed in the קטנה case, so stating it again here looks redundant.

steps.title: Both cases are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers צריכא. From the קטנה case alone, we might think רב rules that way only because there was no condition. Where there is a condition, he might agree with שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary to state both. For if it were stated only in that case, I would say רב ruled that way there because there is no condition. But here, where there is a condition, I might say he agrees with שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the קטנה case is not enough to teach רב's view in our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the קטנה case there was no condition, so it is easy to say the husband meant his relations as קידושין. In our case he deliberately attached a condition, so we might think he still relies on that conditional קידושין and does not intend a new one. That would make רב agree with שמואל, so our case had to be stated to show that רב still says she needs a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary (to state both cases)
In that case (the other one)
There is not / there is
He agrees

steps.whatToRemember: The two disputes are not the same. A condition might have changed רב's view, so his ruling had to be stated in the case with a condition too.

steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכא: showing that each case teaches something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the קטנה case alone, we might think רב would agree with שמואל when there is a condition.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our case had to be stated to teach that רב requires a גט even when there is a condition.

steps.title: The other direction: why the conditional case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: If we had only the conditional קידושין case, we might think שמואל says the relations did not make a marriage only there, because she actually broke a condition. In the קטנה case, where there is no condition, he might agree with רב. So both cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the מחלוקת were stated only in this case of a condition, I would say that only here does שמואל rule that she is not married. But in that other case of the קטנה, I would say he agrees with רב. So it is necessary to state both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its צריכא answer by showing the other direction. Each case teaches something the other case could not teach on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 3 the גמרא showed that the קטנה case alone would not tell us רב's view where there is a condition. Now it shows the reverse: the conditional case alone would not tell us שמואל's view where there is no condition. With a condition that was broken, there is a strong reason to say the relations did not make a real marriage. Without a condition, שמואל might agree with רב that the relations were meant as real קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it were stated (only in one case)
In this case / in that case
Agrees, admits

steps.whatToRemember: צריכא works in both directions. Without the conditional case, we would not know רב's view there. Without the קטנה case, we would not know שמואל's view there. Each case teaches something new.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of the צריכא answer begun in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכא: each case teaches something that cannot be learned from the other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the conditional case alone, we might think שמואל rules this way only because a condition was broken. In the קטנה case he might agree with רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מחלוקת needed to be stated in both cases, so it is not repeated for nothing.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the disagreement between רב and שמואל holds whether or not there was a condition.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: she leaves without a כתובה, so she needs a גט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if he married her without mentioning a condition and vows were found on her, she leaves without a כתובה. It then reads this to mean that she still needs a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: If he married her without saying anything, and it turned out she had vows, she is sent away without a כתובה. The גמרא infers: it is only the כתובה that she does not get, but she does need a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה and draws a careful inference from its wording. This sets up a challenge against שמואל, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says she loses her כתובה. It does not say she leaves with no גט at all. From that silence the גמרא infers that a גט is still required, and a גט is needed only if she was really married.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה
He married her without saying anything about a condition

A bill of divorce (גט)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the צריכא, the גמרא turns to testing the מחלוקת against a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That a woman married without mentioning a condition, who turns out to have vows, still needs a גט
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: כנסה סתם ונמצאו עליה נדרים תצא שלא בכתובה, read carefully: only the כתובה is lost

steps.title: The משנה seems to be talking about our exact case, so it refutes שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה is talking about a man who made קידושין with a condition and then married her without mentioning it. If she needs a גט there, the marriage counts, just as רב said, and שמואל is refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the משנה not talking about a case where he made קידושין on condition and then married her without saying anything? If so, this is a refutation of שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the inference from the משנה to the exact case of the מחלוקת and declares it a strong challenge to שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier part of the משנה dealt with קידושין made on the condition that she has no vows. The גמרא suggests that the next part, "he married her without specifying," continues that same case. If so, the משנה requires a גט even though the condition was broken. That matches רב, who says the relations made a real קידושין, and it goes against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: "What, is it not...?" A suggestion of how to read a source, used to build a challenge
On a condition
A strong refutation

steps.confusionAlert: "מאי לאו" is only a suggested reading. The גמרא often follows it by showing that the source can be read another way. Do not assume שמואל is defeated yet.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first source the גמרא brings to test the מחלוקת, and how it is answered will show how the משנה can be read.
